messages:
linda-support: Customer reports trial credits not decrementing despite successful API calls. Account acct_0931. Usage in billing shows tokens consumed but dashboard credit balance unchanged. Repro steps attached, escalating to billing + infra. cc @matt-eng @kim-billing

matt-eng: Thanks — can you paste raw request + headers (no API key) and the request ids/timestamps? Also is the client using streaming? streaming vs non-streaming endpoints sometimes route through different accounting paths.

linda-support: Repro steps from customer:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
 -H "Content-Type: application/json"
 -d '{"model":"rwkv-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"stream":true,"idempotency-key":"idem-12345"}'
```
They said each request returned 200 and chunks, but UI credits stayed the same. They sent request id `req_20251105_142312`.

billing-bot: Automated: usage event processed for acct_0931: +1,200 tokens at 2025-11-05T14:23:12Z (event_id: ue_7741).

kim-billing: Can we check the ingestion pipeline and reconciliation logs? Two quick questions: 1) did the client set a stable idempotency-key across retries? 2) any errors in the usage consumer during that window (14:20-14:40 UTC)?

matt-eng: Looking at logs for req_20251105_142312 — I see the client used the same idempotency-key across 3 parallel connections. Our dedup logic treats identical idempotency-key + endpoint as a single logical request and skips duplicate accounting events for non-streaming calls, but streaming endpoints create separate partial events. There's a mismatch: streaming requests were being deduped before the streaming event aggregator emitted final usage. Result: tokens were recorded in billing events (we see ue_7741) but the frontend cache never received the final reconciliation notification.

ops: We also had ES throttling and a backlog on the usage-realtime index between 14:22–14:35 UTC; dashboards read from a cached snapshot TTL 30m which meant UI balance could be stale. That explains delayed updates for some customers.

support-engineer: Customer replied — they still see same credit count after 2 hours. Provided screenshot and the three request ids: req_20251105_142312, req_20251105_142313, req_20251105_142314.

matt-eng: Found 2 malformed usage events in kafka for those request ids — the streaming-finalization flag was missing because dedup path removed the finalizer message. I pushed a hotfix to the aggregator to tolerate idempotency collisions on streaming endpoints and emit final usage. Patch deployed to staging; rolling to prod now. Workaround: ask customer to remove idempotency-key or use unique keys per request.

billing-bot: Automated: Reconciliation job ran and corrected +1,200 tokens for acct_0931 at 2025-11-05T15:01:09Z (recon_id: recon_991).

linda-support: Notified customer that credits should now be reflected. They confirmed balance updated and call succeeded. Marking thread resolved. Notes for follow-up: add monitoring alert when reconciliation adjustments >500 tokens within 1h and update docs to warn about idempotency-key reuse with streaming. :white_check_mark:

ops: Filing a short postmortem note and a small dashboard TTL change request to avoid this confusion in future.

matt-eng: Will open a GH issue to tighten dedup logic + add an e2e test for streaming idempotency behavior.
